subject: BrightLane: SDK retry-mode guidance & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Sam Tucker <sam.tucker@brightlane.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, contracts@brightlane.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production retry surge — seeing duplicates, need MAP

Hi Priyom,

We started seeing a spike in duplicated downstream events yesterday after enabling the SDK-based client retry policy. The bulk of our traffic is hitting a variant of the Redwood runtime and about ~0.8% of requests are producing duplicate output (same response content sent twice to our event consumer).

We've attached a small snippet of the error window and a sample of the request/response pair that was duplicated. Can Redwood help with a quick mutual action plan (MAP) — ideally a short-lived config change on your side to suppress non-idempotent client retries or guidance we can apply client-side to avoid duplicates while we prepare a longer-term fix?

Impact: production, US region, affecting a handful of high-value customers. We have an active renewal conversation and want to avoid escalation.

Attachments: brightlane-error-sample-20260621.txt

Thanks,
Sam Tucker
Director of Engineering, BrightLane
sam.tucker@brightlane.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Tucker <sam.tucker@brightlane.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production retry surge — seeing duplicates, need MAP

Team — forwarding BrightLane's window. TL;DR: duplicates tied to client retry policy + route to runtime variant. They asked for a short-lived config or server-side suppression to remediate while they patch clients.

Immediate asks:
- Can Platform expose a temporary flag to suppress non-idempotent retries server-side (so client retry calls still succeed but are deduped)?
- If not, can we route their traffic to a variant with stricter prefix/kvcache isolation for 48 hours?
- Sales: I need a short MAP doc (timeline, who touches what) to reassure BrightLane/legal.

Attaching their error snippet. I'm willing to own customer comms if we have a path.

Attachments: brightlane-error-sample-20260621.txt

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Tucker <sam.tucker@brightlane.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production retry surge — seeing duplicates, need MAP

Thanks for the flag, Priyom. For customer-facing MAP and immediate remediation I propose the following playbook (short-term):

1) Short-term mitigation (hours):
   - Platform: enable per-customer "suppress_non_idempotent_retries" for BrightLane traffic (will dedupe the retry path server-side).
   - SalesEng (Priyom): communicate that this is a 48-hour mitigation while they deploy a client patch.

2) Mid-term (48-72 hours):
   - Route BrightLane to the dedicated variant 'rls-isolated-v2' that has stricter KV cache and sequential token consistency.
   - Platform: run a 10% canary, then 100% if no regressions.

3) Long-term (2+ weeks):
   - Runtime: add an opt-in server-side idempotency token header and SDK integration to avoid relying on behavioral suppression.

Questions for Platform (Karthik/Logan):
- Is the suppress flag something we can toggle per-account at runtime without a code deploy?
- Can we do the canary in the US region by EOD tomorrow?

I'll draft a MAP doc for Sam and include timeline checkpoints and owner names. Priyom — can you confirm whether BrightLane can accept the 48-hour window?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

> On Mon, 22 Jun 2026 at 10:08, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Team — forwarding BrightLane's window...
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Tucker <sam.tucker@brightlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production retry surge — seeing duplicates, need MAP

Acknowledged. Quick runtime assessment:

- Root cause hypothesis: client retries are replaying requests that the runtime currently treats as non-idempotent because we rely on KV cache + ephemeral session keys for dedupe. The effect shows up when a request arrives after the KV cache window has lapsed or when requests land on different-worker groups.

- Short-term server-side option: implement a per-account in-memory dedupe window (suppress_non_idempotent_retries) keyed by (account_id, client_request_id) that will hold entries for ~30s. This is feasible as a config toggle and does not require a full codepath deploy if we use existing feature-flag infrastructure. Risk: small memory overhead per account; we can limit to BrightLane for 48 hours.

- Routing option: moving BrightLane to 'rls-isolated-v2' is safe; it isolates workers and preserves KV affinity so it should reduce duplicates dramatically. Canary plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6-8 hours assuming no elevated error/latency. I can own the canary if Logan can help with metric dashboards.

Actionable timeline (proposed):
- Today (within 4 hours): enable suppress_non_idempotent_retries for BrightLane via flag toggle.
- Tomorrow morning: start canary to rls-isolated-v2 at 10%.
- Within 48 hours: complete move + monitor.

I'll attach a brief ops playbook for the flag toggle and the canary steps. Note: this flag is a mitigation, not a full fix. We should schedule the idempotency token work for an engineering sprint (ETA 2-3 sprints).

Attachments: ops-flag-toggle-playbook.md

Karthik Iyer
Principal, Platform & Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
